findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — `organization_context.member` can be `None` for non-member token/API access, so computing `enable_advanced` unconditionally raises `AttributeError` even when optimized pagination was not requested.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to the audit log's `datetime` field, causing every nonempty optimized response to fail with `TypeError` while building cursors.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The advanced negative-offset branch passes a negative index into Django queryset slicing, which Django rejects, causing crafted negative-offset cursors to return 500 errors.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — `BasePaginator` leaves negative offsets unclamped for previous-page cursors, passing them to unsupported Django queryset slicing across every endpoint using this paginator.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys are Redis SETs, but the new code uses ZSET commands on the same namespace, causing `WRONGTYPE` failures during rolling deployments or while old buffers remain unexpired and interrupting ingestion and flushing.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — `ZUNIONSTORE` uses the default `AGGREGATE SUM`, so duplicate or replayed span payloads have their timestamp scores added and may incorrectly survive `ZPOPMIN` ahead of genuinely newer spans.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:61 — The hard-coded 1,000-span cap replaces configurable `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` enforcement, potentially evicting spans too early or allowing more spans than configured.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 can stop deep redirect chains before reaching their canonical root, splitting sufficiently deep span trees into separately flushed segments.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:123 — Tests use only small sets with identical timestamps and do not exceed 1,000 spans or verify that eviction retains the newest scores, leaving the central new behavior untested.

In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys are Redis SETs, but the new code uses ZSET commands on the same namespace, causing `WRONGTYPE` failures during rolling deployments or while old buffers remain unexpired and interrupting ingestion and flushing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to ZSET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. For example, line 197 changes from `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` to `p.zadd(set_key, ...)`. The key naming pattern `span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{parent_span_id}` remains the same. During a rolling deployment, old code instances would still write SETs while new instances write ZSETs to the same keys, and existing unexpired SET keys in Redis would cause WRONGTYPE errors when the new ZSET commands are executed against them. This is a real compatibility issue during deployment transitions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — `ZUNIONSTORE` uses the default `AGGREGATE SUM`, so duplicate or replayed span payloads have their timestamp scores added and may incorrectly survive `ZPOPMIN` ahead of genuinely newer spans.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE being used at lines 47 and 52 in add-buffer.lua without specifying an AGGREGATE option. By default, Redis ZUNIONSTORE uses AGGREGATE SUM, which means if the same span payload appears multiple times (e.g., due to replays or duplicates), their scores (timestamps) will be summed together. This could result in artificially inflated scores, causing those spans to survive the ZPOPMIN trimming at line 58 when they should potentially be removed. The finding correctly identifies a real behavioral issue with the score aggregation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:61 — The hard-coded 1,000-span cap replaces configurable `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` enforcement, potentially evicting spans too early or allowing more spans than configured.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hard-coded limit of 1000 spans in the Lua script (line 61: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`), while the Python code in buffer.py previously had configurable `max_segment_spans` enforcement that was removed (lines 446-452 deleted). This creates a disconnect where the Lua script enforces a fixed limit that may not match the Python configuration. This is a legitimate architectural concern about configuration consistency, but not a bug per se since the Lua script does enforce a limit - it's just not configurable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 can stop deep redirect chains before reaching their canonical root, splitting sufficiently deep span trees into separately flushed segments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit in add-buffer.lua being reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 (line 30). The original comment explicitly states 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1,000, span trees with redirect chains deeper than 1,000 will now fail to be joined correctly, potentially splitting them into separate segments. This is a real correctness issue - the change reduces the maximum supported tree depth from 10,000 to 1,000 without any apparent justification in the diff for why this is safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:123 — Tests use only small sets with identical timestamps and do not exceed 1,000 spans or verify that eviction retains the newest scores, leaving the central new behavior untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces significant new behavior in add-buffer.lua: a 1000-span limit with zpopmin eviction (lines showing 'if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)'). The test file changes only add the required end_timestamp_precise field to existing test cases but don't add any new tests that verify: (1) the 1000-span limit enforcement, (2) that zpopmin correctly evicts oldest spans based on timestamp scores, or (3) behavior when exceeding the limit. This is a valid observation that important new functionality lacks test coverage.
